Consider a steam power plant using a reheat cycle as shown. Steam leaves the boiler and enters the turbine at 4 MPa, [latex]350^{\circ}C[/latex]
 ([latex]h_{3}[/latex]
 = 3095 kJ/kg). After expansion in the turbine to 400 kPa ([latex]h_{4}[/latex]
 = 2609 kJ/kg), the steam is reheated to [latex]350^{\circ}C[/latex]
 ([latex]h_{5}[/latex]
 = 3170 kJ/kg), and then expanded in a low pressure turbine to 10 kPa ([latex]h_{6}[/latex]
 = 2165 kJ/kg). The specific volume of liquid handled by the pump can be assumed to be The thermal efficiency of the plant neglecting pump work is
questions.explanation: Given data: [latex] \begin{array}{l} h_{3}=3095 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{4}=2604 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{5}=3170 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{6}=2165 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{g} \\ h_{1}=29.3 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{array}[/latex] Network output per kg [latex] \begin{aligned} w_{\text {net }} &=\left(h_{3}-h_{4}\right)+\left(h_{5}-h_{6}\right) \\ &=(3095-2609)+(3170-2165) \\ &=1491 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex] Net heat supplied, [latex] \begin{aligned} q_{s} &=\left(h_{3}-h_{2}\right)+\left(h_{5}-h_{4}\right) \\ &=h_{3}-h_{1}+h_{5}-h_{4} \quad \because h_{2} \approx h \\ &=3095-29.3+3170-2609 \\ &=3626.7 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex] Thermal efficiency, [latex] \begin{aligned} \eta &=\frac{w_{\mathrm{net}}}{q_{\mathrm{s}}}=\frac{1491}{3626.7} \\ &=0.4111=41.11 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

Network output per kg

Net heat supplied,
